utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bos, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Bos: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness NN.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have some questions to ask this morning. Witness NN I'd like to take you to the 15th of April, 1993. Is it correct that that was the day that you were trying to get to Jablanica and that you were stopped at the checkpoint at Jablanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, good morning, Your Honours. I don't have any objections. I would kindly ask if there is anything that can be done for me not to watch the witness as if he was on a videolink. Can the partition be moved a little so I can see the witness? As things stand now, I have a feeling that I'm watching him on a TV screen via a videolink. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think Madam Registrar will do her best to accommodate your request, subject to the protective measures. Is that okay? Yes, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness NN. Now, do you recall on that same morning, Witness NN, on the 15th of April, that there was a woman that -- who was in labour and this was the wife after man named Suco Bradaric and that somebody had to find the nurse to assist that woman in her labour? The name of the nurse was nurse Slavica? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know that -- of a nurse whose name was Slavica in Doljani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't recall that on that day somebody had to look for that nurse because the wife of a man named Suco Bradaric was in labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's talk about when you went to that checkpoint. Is it correct that the name of that checkpoint is the Bokulja checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name is Bokulja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry for the pronunciation. Bokulja. Witness, how long did that checkpoint already exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that form, it was put up on that same day, on that very morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean in that form? I mean, did it exist in another form? What was the difference?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From time to time, while convoys were passing through, the convoys of refugees, there were checkpoints put up by the police. The army and the HVO. And this is where checks were done from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, Witness NN, that this Bokulja checkpoint was about 200 metres away from the headquarters of the ABiH in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, isn't it also correct that this Bokulja checkpoint was attacked before by the HVO on the 19th of September, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that not correct or you would just not remember it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct, because we never attacked anybody in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know that the day before, on the 14th of April, that the village of Ostrozac was attacked by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, I put it to you that the HVO did attack that village on the day before and actually successfully took over the village of Ostrozac and if the witness can be shown Exhibit P2 once again? We can zoom in a little bit on the municipality of Jablanica. Witness NN, could you indicate with the pointer where the village of Ostrozac is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it correct, sir, that this village is right on the road to Konjic and that in that sense it's a very strategic position and that if you would take over that village, that you would cut the road from Konjic to Jablanica with the result that the ABiH, if it would need any forces from Konjic, that these forces were Konjic would not be able to reach Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you are discussing military issues. I am not well informed about those, nor was I -- nor did I have anything to do with that. I was a member of the civilian segment of the HVO, so I cannot discuss military issues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Witness NN, the points I'm trying to make is this: The fact that you were not let through at the Bokulja checkpoint, could that not have been the reason that the ABiH was afraid for an imminent attack on Jablanica because the village of Ostrozac was taken the day before and that they were actually afraid for an attack by the Croats, and that was the reason why they didn't let you through in Jablanica on the 15th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that concern.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's move on, on that same day, the 15th of April. You testified that you -- that there were some negotiations with ABiH representatives on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not representatives, but our man who was in Jablanica, Mirko Zelenika, who was not a member of the military part of the HVO but he went to the military command of the army to warn about the things that had been done, that a blockade had been thrown. As for the negotiations at a military level, it was not possible because our military representatives were not in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, sir, didn't you testify that you spoke to a man named Zalih Sihirlic and Mr. Salih Jusic on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They arrived in Doljani on the 16th to talk things over in our command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, they arrived, was it at their initiative that these talks took place? Did they take the initiative to come to Doljani and talk about the situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The initiative of -- was on our part, Mr. Mirko Zelenika went to the army command, asked for the blockade to be lifted and for something to be done in that part. And on his request, on Mirko Zelenika's request, it is probably that these gentlemen came to Doljani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any international observers present for these talks as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that the Spanish Battalion had a quarter in Jablanica at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an UNPROFOR base in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was -- this UNPROFOR base was manned by the Spanish Battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember who was it at the time because they changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the UNPROFOR initiate any negotiations after the conflict had started on the 15th of April, in the days following that -- following the 15th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P325?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness NN, this is an UNPROFOR, a Spanish Battalion report, and I would like you to look at page number 5 of this report, which discusses the situation in Jablanica. It has -- it's headed "Jablanica." Can you see that? It's on page 4 of the B/C/S version. I think you have it in front of you. Now, Witness NN, I'd like you to read -- maybe it's easier if I read it out to you, which it starts at the on the B/C/S version at the bottom paragraph, and it reads as follows: "According to the intelligence received at 2113 OOB, April, 1993," which will probably be 28 April, "From HVO sources the offensive launched against Slatina and Doljani aims to push on through to Jablanica. The offensive is directed by a person of substantial political, economic and military influence. Someone who is tired of signatures and political treaties. Hence he has no wish to up hold the ceasefire agreement struck between the Armija and the HVO. This person is known as Tuta and has chosen two collaborators he had with him in the "Operation Bura," namely Ivan Andabak and brigadier Lasic." Witness, what would be your comment on this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply don't know what was going on in Slatina. I did not have any contacts with them, and as for the break through towards Jablanica, what this implies, I don't know. This was out of the question. Because we were in a defence position. We defended ourselves. And as far as I know, the commander of the entire operation was the commander of the southeast zone, i.e. the Main Staff, because there were several units involved. Therefore, to my mind, this does not reflect the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this paragraph also talks about a ceasefire agreement struck between the Armija and the HVO. Do you know anything about this ceasefire agreement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P138.2, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I would just like to draw the Chamber's attention to something that has been happening on a number of occasions. The original of the text which will be either Spanish or it is indeed on the original, the names that I can read here are "Andavak," with a "V," and in the translation, it reads "Andabak," with a "B."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, we know that. You've made this point every time the document comes out, in English it's Andabak with a V. We know that you've made your point. We haven't forgotten it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, excuse me. Your Honour, I am insisting on this thing. This is not the way how translations can be done. Translators are not here to interpret or to imply what it says. They have to copy the names for what they are. I am waiting to say something about yesterday's testimony. The interpreters are not here to interpret, and think how what somebody's name is. They have to interpret what they hear correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I believe this is not the first time you blame the interpreters for the mistranslation. I certainly will convey your objections to the interpretation section and ask them to check it once again. Well, Mr. Bos, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before you you have Exhibit 318.2, we will keep this document under seal because your name appears on it, but if you read the exhibit, and I won't read it out loud, it says that you, together with Stipe Pole and Ivan Rogic are to attend negotiations and that you will be taken -- well, I'll read out some of it, "They should come to the collapsed part of the road at around 10.00 where they will be taken over by the UNPROFOR. Negotiations will take place in Jablanica with an HVO representatives from Mostar." Witness, and this is signed by the operative zone officer, Mr. Bozo Raguz. Witness, do you recall this message?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see this message for the first time now and I'm not surprised to see my name here, the reason is that I was the representative of the civilian authorities in Jablanica municipality, and therefore, they probably assumed that I had some influence, because I -- my job in -- I perform my duties in Jablanica municipality well, together with all the others. So people from the operation zone assumed that I should be there, and that in that way, some things would be negotiated smoothly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying that you didn't go to those negotiations which are mentioned here in this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The French booth is saying that the second witness's microphone be switched on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Maybe you could also take -- bring Exhibit P318.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, witness, this is an electronic message of the same date, the 20th of April 1993 it has for Mico, Slavko and Tuta, European observers and the Spanish Battalion departed in the direction of Jablanica, signed Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. by Stanko Maric." Witness, first of all, would you know who Mico Slavko and Tuta are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Mr. Tuta. Mico, I assume that this is the commander of the operation zone, Mr. Miljenko Lasic, and Slavko, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could Slavko be Mr. Slavko Puljic, the deputy commander of the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the information that the Spanish Battalion is departing in the direction of Jablanica, could it have anything to do with the message that I showed you earlier that negotiations were being held in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P8.8?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, just briefly, I would like to find out, I waited for the Prosecutor to finish the examination, documents P13.1 and P318.2, what is the source? These are new documents. The source here is ICTY witness. I would like to find out from the Prosecutor which case was it in which these exhibits were admitted in evidence, what witness was that, in which case? We can go to private session. I didn't -- I wasn't aware that somebody was already tried for Sovici before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos? Could you please shed some light on this point? If you need the private session, we will simply go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, to be honest I'm not really sure why it says ICTY witness. If I could come back to this question maybe after the break, because I would have to find out, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just for the record, the original in Croatian has nothing, but the wording, the text, no addressee, no date, no signature, no stamp, just the text, send -- whatever it says, the Spanish Battalion has been sent for negotiations and the signatures Stanko Maric, that is all, in the Croatian original, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, a photograph has been put on the overhead projector, and I would like to ask you, do you recognise the building which is depicted on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The church, the priest's residence, and the command of the battalion. The village of Sarancevici and further down the village of Basici, Stupari is up in the hills over here. Over here the village of Orlovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you've pointed at this house which you've called the HVO headquarters. Was this the house which was also referred to as the fish farm? Or did it used to be a fish farm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see the ponds in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when was it that the -- you've testified that the civil component of the HVO moved into this headquarters sometime in April. When was it in April that you moved into these headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we could no longer go to Jablanica, then we found some accommodation in the priest's residence in the basement, and in part also we accommodated the Defence office here. That is the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the 3rd Mijat Tomic Battalion, had they had their headquarters here as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you've said that -- I don't think you've answered my question yet. When was it that you moved from Jablanica to Doljani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we could no longer go, after the 15th of April, when we could not get in, we found some shelter here. We simply needed to have some premises, some offices, to look after the interests of our civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But isn't it correct that you moved already earlier, around early April, not only the civil component but also other HVO troops moved to Doljani in early April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 1st of April, the battalion command moved to Doljani, and we, the civilian component, we continued going to Jablanica for work regularly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you said the battalion command moved, how many officers, how many bodies actually moved to Doljani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that. I wasn't really fully abreast of the organisation of the battalion or its command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you know even an approximate number? Are we talking about dozens or are we talking about just a few men or ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our command had never more than ten people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, was this the place, this HVO headquarters, where you actually saw Mr. Tuta on the 19th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know a man by the name of Alojz Rados?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes, I met him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything much about Mr. Alojz Rados in our villages, Sovici, Doljani and Jablanica. All Rados's are Muslims and the first time I heard about him was in Jablanica, that was the first time I heard that there was Rados, that he had come from the municipality of Varos, from Central Bosnia, and joined -- that he had joined a unit of the 3rd Battalion of Mijat Tomic. I did not have any particular contact with him because I simply didn't know him that well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what his function was in the Mijat Tomic Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he had any function in the Mijat Tomic Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that he also worked at the headquarters in Doljani where you were also stationed in April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used to see him, but it was more often when -- in that town, where Mr. Miroslav Juric who headed the Catholic charities society, the two of them were more committed to humanitarian work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, in your position, you -- I presume you often had meetings. Do you recall that this Mr. Rados ever took minutes of the meetings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know that Mr. Rados kept a diary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard about a diary from our prisoners in Jablanica. Later on, when they came out, they stayed that on the local cable television, they had read some diary written by Mr. Alojz Rados. I did not have an opportunity to see it personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying that prisoners in Jablanica talked -- what did they say about it? What was their comments about the fact that this diary was written?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, simply I wasn't interested to know what was in it but all sorts were being written down and at the same time we had the opportunity to listen to daily media campaigns launched by the press service of the 4th Corps of the Army of BH, so that I wasn't really particularly eager to know what was in this diary and I never paid any particular attention to it, because right from the start, I accepted that it was just one of a number of media campaigns.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 928/3?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'm going to show you a segment from this diary because your name has been referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. It is a procedural matter, and I believe I am entitled to an objection to the further examination of the Prosecution about this diary. That is Rule 95 says that the evidence obtained by methods which -- that such rules are not accepted, that rules as a result are not acceptable. Will also not be admissible. We also have another ruling in a different case. The question is what will happen to this part of the transcript, of the record, which is based on the cross-examination about this diary which is an exhibit obtained unlawfully and moreover it has not been authenticated because it has not -- because that was not done by its author? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I apologise for taking too much of your time because I have a feeling that we, the counsel for the Defence, stand up very often in performance of our duty but do so to no avail, but I don't know what else, if the Prosecutor himself doesn't know where he got this diary from, nor could he explain the source to the Court. Your Honours, I shall be very pragmatic and say, couldn't the Defence write an identical diary or acquire it, put a Muslim name on it and say that this is a diary which comes from Sovici and then examine the witnesses? I am asking the Honourable Court not to allow any further examination based on this diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that we have come across this issue before. I don't think we have to deal with it whenever we are using this diary in the future. I think during the last time we had considerable debate on this issue, and the Trial Chamber even invited both parties to submit their views concerning the interpretations of the BiH government. This Trial Chamber is seized of this motion of admission of those evidence, and we haven't decided yet on this very issue. But we allowed the Prosecution to use this document because we found no suggestions that this document obtained through illegal way, and it does not hurt the integrity of this trial. So Mr. Bos, you may proceed with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May I just add? This witness has been asked questions about the diary, to confirm the authenticity of the diary. And that's why I actually put the diary to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I have already noted that, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you have a look at -- I'm going to put to you two segments from this diary. You could look at the B/C/S version page number 13 and the English version page number 65 on the bottom And I'll read it out to you, and I won't mention your name again. English version starting from the bottom. "Then a signals man came in. He told to us get the doctor urgently because the wife of somebody called Suco Bradaric in signals was in labour. [redacted] and I went out to look for the doctor and wake him up. But he sent us to look for nurse Slavica. Because he was not a gynecologist and knew nothing about the deliveries." Then your name is mentioned. You and the doctor managed to find Slavica before we did and a new life a son was born, one day after the start of the war." Witness, this was on the 15th of April. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall this because, as I said, I went to Jablanica, and Mr. Prosecutor, [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I think we need a redaction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please try to refrain from mentioning your name, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Mr. Prosecutor, you also read out the name. So please don't do it again, from the diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: He said, "Your name is mentioned, you and the doctor managed to find."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. He said -- mentioned the name, the first name, not the last name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll try to redact whatever seems suspicious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Witness. I understand your response. You may be rights. There could be others. Could we then move on to --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: May I ask a question, Mr. Bos, just while we are on the diary? Mr. Witness, you are somewhat acquainted with the author of the diary, I believe. You may not know him well but you know who he was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the early days of our organisation in Jablanica, I was the first time when I heard of Mr. Alojz Rados's name as a Croat from Varos. I did not know him before that, nor did I come to know him particularly well after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I accept that, sir, but all I wanted to know was did -- do you know or did you know what he did in civilian life, what his Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. occupation was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, he was employed by a hydro power plant but what he did, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. I was looking at the diary last night and I noticed that there are a lot of minute measurements recorded and it struck me that it was a rise and fall in water levels, so that explains it. You think that he worked for the hydro electric plant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to read out one more quote to you from this diary and maybe just out of abundance of caution we could go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more topic. For that I need Exhibit P333.1. Witness, while this exhibit is being put to you, may I ask you, do you know Marko Rozic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. He's a guy who comes from the village of Sovici. Before the war he worked for Unis and that was my company too. At present, he is with Elektroprivreda in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time of the conflict, was Mr. Rozic, was he the deputy of the -- was he the head of the HVO Defence department in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you've testified in your examination-in-chief that both the mosques were destroyed in Sovici and Doljani and that you regret that, and that also Muslim houses were torched, that ABiH prisoners were taken to Ljubuski. That is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you read this report and say if you actually agree with what's written here in the report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of this report, and I disagree with its text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what would you disagree with? The text talks about the fact that 94 military recruits from sent to Ljubuski. Would you disagree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was their number, I don't know, whether this is the accurate number or not, I don't know. I'm not objecting to that. However, I am objecting to the fact that the civilians were brought together, were rounded in and together. My objection is to the place where it says that all Muslim houses had been set on fire, which is not true. Not even after the war, when everything stopped, not all of them were torched, and about the order from some commander, I really am not aware that all this was done pursuant to some order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that not all Muslim houses were torched. Approximately how many Muslim houses were torched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, perhaps -- no, I'm saying of course roughly. Perhaps half of them. 50 per cent. At the time when this report was made. I say it was very rough guess. I cannot be more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say 50 per cent, what would be the number of houses, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Any re-examination? Mr. Krsnik? Re-examined by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only one. Witness will you please look at this so-called report once again? Are you familiar with Mr. Rozic's signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, there is no signature here on this text, on the text that I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then why aren't you given the original in the Croatian, if we are talking about the same exhibit, P333? Is this P333? Then you obviously don't have it. Could the registry provide the witness with the Croatian original?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I believe that re-examination should be within the scope of the cross-examination. The document P333 was not used in the cross-examination, so Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could clarify something, P333 and P33.1 are the same document we submitted both of them but they come from different sources but they are identical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Is it necessary to submit the same document twice?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just in order to show the authentication of the document we thought it better to submit both documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But one -- it seems to me that one document has the signature on it and the other is a kind of fax or telex type document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: That's why we submitted both. The other reason is that one version of the B/C/S is less readable than the others. That's why we submitted both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. In this case, Mr. Krsnik, you may use the document P333.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, and my thanks in particular go to Mr. Bos -- to my learned friend, to Mr. Bos, and his integrity, his honesty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, will you now look at this document which is before you? My question was whether you were familiar with Mr. Rozic's signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if this is his signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give an expert opinion and confirm that this is not Mr. Rozic's signature? Thank you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I have no further questions. He is not an expert, that is true, and that is why we shall submit the signature for an expert analysis and then an expert will tell us that this is a forged signature. The witness only said that he knew Mr. Rozic's signature and that this signature here was not his. You don't have to object any more. I do not have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos? Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object on a procedural point we covered this ground many times now. The Chamber has repeatedly admonished counsel not to have these discussions in front of the witness. The counsel has just said in front of a witness on a matter that is been the subject of cross-examination and direct examination, and given substantive information and made allegations of forgery, unsupported, completely unsupported in front of the witness. Now, the Chamber bore has repeatedly cautioned and admonished Mr. Krsnik on this. We object to it strenuously and we are going to continue to do so and if it happens we're going to ask that the witness be excused every time we get into a discussion along these lines, have the witness excused so these discussions will not take place in front of the witness. We object very strongly to this, Mr. President, and you know it's not the first time it's been raised and we raised it repeatedly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I admit that I am not really at home with the Anglo-Saxon procedure. So please forgive me for what I will say, but I do not think that even in the Anglo-Saxon system a trial is a theatre. It is a live hearing and it is the pursuit of truth. Why is it wrong to ask the witness if, "Do you know somebody's signature?" And you say yes and so do you think it is his signature and he says no? What is curious about that and what is the Defence doing that is wrong? These are the documents that were used by the other party. And Your Honours, I'm saying this for yet another reason and that is that the Prosecutor had the documents about the order about the transfer of civilians, that he disclosed to us personally and he knows also the other side of the Sovici events and still continues to insist on something completely different, and therefore the Defence must produce all the evidence and offer it on a platter to them and to you Your Honours for all the that they had filed to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you asked the witness a question and the witness answered that question, he answered no. You have to -- you have the full right to raise this issue concerning the authenticity of a document when we are admitting it into the evidence. And you also have the opportunity to submit any written objections at a later stage, to help the Trial Chamber to arrive at the correct decisions on this issue. So I think you have finished your re-examination. So we have to move on. We tried to finish the testimony of this witness during this sitting. Yes, any questions from Judges? Well, it seems that we have no questions to this witness. Witness, thank you very much for coming to give your evidence. When the usher pulls down the blinds, she will take you out of the room. We all wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you for giving me the opportunity to testify and I kindly ask you to do establish the truth about the sufferings of Croats in Jablanica municipality. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender? Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. These are the ones that I have used, these are P362 and P360. Then orders by General Milivoj Petkovic about the evacuation of the population from Jablanica on the 5th of May. These are the -- this is the order that the Prosecution had a long time ago, P360 and P362 are the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I would also tender D1/392 to 397.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution does not have any objections to P360 and P362, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course, that's your exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: As to the Defence exhibits, the witness was shown these documents and he could hardly say anything about the documents. He could simply say, well, yeah, this was sort of the situation as it was. I don't think that is sufficient to admit these exhibits and we can put this in writing if you wish but we would object to those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: On your side how many documents are you going to tender at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would tender Exhibit P318.1, and P318.2, and Exhibit P-- yes, those are the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Just two documents. Are there any objections, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I do have objections. In the same way that my learned friend objected to my -- to me, from the very beginning of this trial, the Prosecution has been showing these written documents and in 90 per cent of the cases, the witnesses didn't know anything about these documents and still, the Prosecution wanted them to be admitted. And this gentleman said that the events described in the documents, he was familiar with. So Your Honours, as far as the Exhibit 318.1 is concerned and 318.2, we have established Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that as far as 318.1 is concerned, that the document and the signature on the document -- I apologise. 318.1, 318.2, these are the documents that I'm talking about. We don't have the authors of these documents, the addressees, why they were sent, there is no signature, there is no stamp, and especially, 318.2, actually the two are identical. We don't know who the addressee is, who wrote them, they do have a date but still, I believe that such documents cannot be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have already made that objection during the cross-examination, Mr. Krsnik. And we will take into consideration the objections of both parties, and we will render our decisions on the admission of these documents at a later stage. Could we -- are there any protective measures concerning the next witness, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, as previously, a pseudonym and face distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections? I guess no. So your request is granted. And we will make a break here and after the break, we will hear the next witness. Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I forgot to tender the photo that the witness was looking at, and put an arrow on it. That's Exhibit -- can the Madam Registrar help me with the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, so that is the exhibit that I would like to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't think there any objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It is admitted into evidence. So we'll resume at 20 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: While they are getting the witness I would just like to see if you verified that Defence counsel have a meeting at 12.30 today, 1.30, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will stop earlier, 20 minutes earlier. Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we don't -- I'm quite confident that we never received a witness summary for the next witness so I think I've got a decent idea of what he's going to say but if we could get an idea of the length of time that's anticipated for his direct examination, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik? Would you please brief us on that point?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honours. My learned friend Stringer asked me yesterday when I got home yesterday afternoon, I spoke to my assistant, Mrs. Pinter, and she answered me that she had sent these -- this summary a long time ago. She also promised she would call Mr. Stringer, whether she did or not, he can tell us. She was supposed to do that yesterday afternoon. So the summary -- so the summary must have been received by Mr. Stringer. I'm 100 per cent sure of that. And as for the length of my examination, I can only say this depends on the witness. This is our joint witness. Both for Mr. Martinovic as well as for Mr. Naletilic. So Mr. Seric is also going to examine the witness. I can only assume that it will take up to an hour altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we have to proceed since we have the witness waiting outside at this stage. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this is the way to do it so you don't lose your headphones. Is that okay now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the most important thing in this courtroom is that our -- my question and your answer do not overlap. Please look at the screen in front of you. You're going to see the moving dot. Make sure that you don't speak too slow or too fast. When the dot stops, -- now it has stopped, then it would be best for you to start giving your answer. We have two interpretations and it is very important that everything you say is entered in the transcript. Is that agreed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you're going to be given a piece of paper, don't say your name. You have protective measures. If this is your name, just say yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's get down to business, just briefly, without saying your first name and your last name, slowly, can you tell us when you were born, where, just briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I was born on 14 December, 1970 in Mostar. I finished elementary and secondary school in Siroki Brijeg. I am married and I have three children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to focus on 1993, and to be more specific on one period only. That is the period between May, 1993 and the end of 1993. My first question to you is as follows: Which duty did you discharge, if you had any duties, throughout 1993? Slowly, please. Now it has stopped.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: In 1993, I was the commander of the first active battalion of the military police. Then I was the commander of one of the sectors in the city of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please move to private session, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are now in open session. Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Mr. Stringer for this warning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the night between the 8th and 9th May I spent the night in the family house in Siroki Brijeg and in the early morning hours of the 9th of May, I was woken up by my duty operations officer from the command of the 1st Battalion and he informed me that the units of the BH Army had attacked the HVO units in the city of Mostar. I got into my private car and immediately went to my command in Ljubuski, where I organised a meeting with my subordinate officers, already by then we had received an order to -- for me to take my unit to the city of Mostar and to help the HVO units which were in the city of Mostar at the time. And to help them in their fighting the HB army. I arrived in Mostar. I can't remember exactly when, but I believe it was in the early afternoon hours. I believe it was around 1300 hours. In Mostar, at the time, there was fierce fighting between the HVO and the units of the BH Army. The HV units were not organised. They tried to put up a defence against the BH Army units. I remember that later that afternoon, the situation was stabilised. The front line was stabilised and that the fighting started only on the 10th of May in the afternoon, and that it was then that the front line was established in the city of Mostar along the Bulevar, along the -- along Santic street, up to the Ero Hotel. Then on the right bank of the Neretva River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness I'm reading the transcript and I can tell you that we now have HV, that HV units were not organised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I meant HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My colleague is probably going to ask you to give more details of that line, but let me now ask you how old were you at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I was 22 at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you, so young, were appointed to that position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I was appointed because I -- I suppose I had some authority, I had organisational capabilities. I was not appointed because somebody liked me. The times were too hard to have somebody discharging that duty because he was either liked or not liked by somebody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was your command, the command of your sector?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: The command of the military police at the time was at the school of mechanical engineering so my command also, at the time, when I was in Mostar, the command of the 1st Battalion was this mechanical -- school of mechanical engineering, and the command of the sector was also at the school of mechanical engineering.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that we have mentioned the school of mechanical engineering, Witness, we have heard in this courtroom some testimonies involving this school of mechanical engineering. My first question to you will be as follows: Who -- which units were headquartered at the school of mechanical engineering and who could enter the school of mechanical engineering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: The unit of the military police was there, and nobody could enter the school of mechanical engineering. There was security. And there was a book kept by the duty operations officer, a policeman, who would record everybody who entered or left school of mechanical engineering.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I tell you that we have heard some testimonies hear saying that the Convicts Battalion was abusing some prisoners at the school of mechanical engineering --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: At the school of mechanical engineering, there were never any military prisoners, and I don't see how could anybody abuse or maltreat prisoners who were not there, let alone the Convicts Battalion, which was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. not in Mostar at the time at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we are talking about this, can you tell us which units, I believe that the Chamber will be interested in that, which HVO units were in Mostar between the 30 June and onwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Your Honours, at the time, in Mostar, there were the following units, there was the 2nd Brigade of the HVO, parts of the 3rd Brigade of the HVO, for a while there was also the 9th Battalion of the 3rd Brigade which then was pulled out of the city and throughout all this time, there was the 4th Battalion of the 3rd Brigade at the time, this were no guards brigades so it was just the 3rd Brigade. There was also the Vinko Skrobo ATG, the Benko Penavic ATG and the military police unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that some battalions were resubordinated from some brigades. Did I understand you well? Can you explain that for the Chamber? If somebody -- if somebody battalion is resubordinated from a brigade and it arrives in the city of Mostar, who is their commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: All the units on the front line were commanded by me personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, I don't know whether this happened or not, just to illustrate, let's say that an ATG arrived from Sarajevo or Tomislavgrad, and they arrived to your front line. Who would be their commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I've already answered you, counsel. I would be their commander, as the commander of the defence sector in the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just briefly, can you tell us, because my learned friends are going to ask you about that, can you give me the general outlines of the areas of responsibility of these units that you have just mentioned and who has established these areas of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: What period do you ever in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 30th of June onwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: In the city of Mostar at the time the 2nd Brigade of the HVO comprised the area from the school of engineering in Santiceva street north all the way up to Bijelo Polje. Then parts of the military police, together with the 2nd Battalion of the 2nd Brigade of the HVO were in Santiceva street, around the building of the former HIT department store and the Glas bank. That was the area that belonged to the civilian police. Then the grammar school southwards, the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just asked you for the general outlines. I believe that my colleagues are going to go into details on that. So you said from Bijelo Polje to --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes, from Bijelo Polje south to Santiceva street. That was the 2nd Brigade of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then briefly, there were also units from the Ero Hotel down to south to Hum Hill. These were the mixed units, parts of the 3rd Brigade. HVO ATG units, parts of the military police and parts of the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But you didn't tell me who defined the areas of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: These areas of responsibility were defined by the operative zone of Southeast Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Now, just in principle, because we do not want to take too much time, who commanded Vinko Skrobo ATG and Benko Penavic ATG in the city of Mostar and what does ATG mean? Will you tell the Honourable Court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Vinko Penavic -- Benko Penvic and Vinko Skrobo ATG and all the others units that were in the city of Mostar at the time were under my command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right but individually who was the commander of Benko Penavic and Vinko Skrobo and what would ATG mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Vinko Skrobo's commander was Mr. Martinovic and Benko Penavic's commander, I know that several commanders were there, but one of them was Mr. Mario Milicevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And ATG means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I think it means the anti-terrorist unit, and I believe that these groups, that is units, which were called that, were named that modeled on one of the special NATO units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean to get to become a more important to them or were they really special units, if I puts it that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Well, a little bit to add some more weight to their importance but also there were somewhat more brave than other units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they themselves called them ATG. Nobody else gave them that name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that you were the commander of all the units on the fronts line

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I think that perhaps we should go into private session while we are discussing these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me, when you met him, at that time, did Mr. Mladen Naletilic hold any office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I met him as a man who had worked in Germany for a long time and who had returned to his native town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And later on, in 1992, did he join the defence or do you know anything else? I mean of your personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: What I know is that in 1992, Mr. Naletilic was one of the organisers of the defence in Siroki Brijeg, together with Mr. Cavar, Mr. Mikulic, and others who were in the Siroki Brijeg HVO at the time, and that he made a large contribution to the organisation of this defence. I also know that the later stage, he contributed a great deal to the liberation of the city of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Tell me, please, did Mr. Naletilic -- with you, together with you, plan any operation in Mostar in 1993, and in particular, in September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No. He did not. Mr. Naletilic did not plan any operation in Mostar with me at any time in 1993. As far as I know, Mr. Mladen Naletilic at that time was doing something, held some office, in the Siroki Brijeg municipal hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, of these ATGs, for instance, and these units, and you, was there somebody else? Was there another tier in the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No, nothing, the commanders of these units were directly accountable to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were under the command of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: And I was under the command of the commander of the operative zone or the Chief of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is there anyone else in between?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Mladen Naletilic attend any meeting in the command of the operative zone or the command of the city defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No, never. I never saw him at any meeting. I do not see why would Mr. Naletilic attend those meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have an office in the operative zone or rather the command of the operative zone or the city defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Counsel, sir, I've already answered that, why would he have an office if that office served no purpose? Of course he didn't have an office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who had the authority over the military investigative prison at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I know that the military investigative prison at the Heliodrom was guarded by the military police, but I really do not remember who had the authority. I assume it was one of the ministries. Could be the Ministry of Justice or the Ministry of Defence but I really do not know under whose jurisdiction it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did any unit, and that includes the Convicts Battalion, could arrest somebody or capture somebody and take him directly to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: All units, if they captured or took in some military prisoners, all the prisoners of war would be turned over to the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you know something about the Rastani front line, Rastani front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes. I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, is Rastani an integral part of the Mostar defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: For a while, it was an integral part of the defence of the city of Mostar, but from what I can remember, for a while, it was separated, it was an independent sector. I believe it was sometime from the end of August, 1993, but I do not remember precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did this Rastani front line have its own commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did all the units -- were all the units that will be assigned to that front line, be then subordinated to that commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: , Mr. President, I would have objected to the last question as leading. The witness had already answered by the time that I got the interpretation, but I will object to leading questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik, try to avoid any leading questions in your future direct examination. I understand you are under time pressure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, by all means, Your Honour, of course I will do that. But I think there must have been a misunderstanding because in the previous answer this witness has already indicated everything about it. I only asked him to confirm that units would then be subordinated to that particular commander if this explanation is satisfactory. But whatever the case, I will not ask any other leading questions in the future.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please, do you know a place called Djubrani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Djubrani is a place which is about a kilometre and a half or two away from Rastani as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. thing. And to protect the civilians regardless of whether they were Muslims or Croats or Serbs, to protect all the citizens living in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my final question is: Have you received recently an invitation to meet with the investigators of The Hague OTP and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I did get such an invitation -- such a letter from The Hague OTP, and it was transmitted to me by the SNS officer. This is the state security service of the Croat people which is responsible, which is accountable to the member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina from amongst the ranks of the Croat people, and I responded that I was a witness for the defence and that all the questions that the OTP would want to ask me, I would be at their disposal when I went as a witness for the defence to The Hague, to which this officer replied that "this was my last chance," which I failed to understand what did this "last chance" mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: It happened about a month ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he perhaps mention who was asking for this interview, whose order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No, he did not mention any names. He only said OTP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this SNS, since we are on this subject now, is it the same thing as -- would it be the counterpart of the AID from amongst the ranks of the Bosniak people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes. It's the same like the one from the ranks of the Bosnian people except that it is accountable to the member of the Presidency representing the Croat people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the AID?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Member of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina representing the Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] No further questions, Your Honour. Thank you. [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Seric:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. NO, can you tell us who commanded the sector prior to the 30th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: At that time, there were no any particular sectors in the city of Mostar, the units at that time were under the command of the operative -- of the Southeast Herzegovina operative zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about the terms of reference of the commander this sector of the defence of the city of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Well, the terms of reference, the mandate of the commander of the sector of defence of the city of Mostar were to command all the units which were in the sector of the city of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will redact that part. And at the same time, I have to warn you that you have to slow down so that the interpreters could follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. NO, do you know when did the Vinko Skrobo ATG come into being and how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Well, I cannot give you the exact date of its establishment but I believe it was sometime in mid-May, after the first major attacks of the BH Army on HVO units in the city of Mostar, and I think that it was made up of volunteers, those more valiant combatants, who stood out in particular in the war against the Serb aggressor in 1992, because that was principally how all -- basically how all the ATG units were formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask the usher, please, Madam Registrar, will you -- can provide, this is Prosecutor's photograph 14.5, 14.5, Prosecution's exhibit, so that we can show it to the witness? We can also have it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you will take the pointer, -- could we have a clean copy, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, that's just what I want to ask. I see some marks on this photo. Do we have a clean copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. NO, will you take the pointer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you now show the positions manned by Vinko Skrobo ATG on this front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: At that time, on the front line, the Vinko Skrobo ATG held the health centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you point at it on the ELMO itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: So the health centre buildings around the health centre, and its other position, so this is the contact line. And its other position was where the headquarters was of the Vinko Skrobo ATG. You cannot see it on this map. It is a few hundred metres, that is 500 or 600 metres away from the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you, for the record, describe on the photograph, can you describe the buildings that you pointed on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Well, these are the buildings of the health centre and behind it are some -- I do not really know what they were called at the time, this couple of buildings, which are behind the health centre. And the whole yard of the health centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, which -- what is the name of the street left of the health centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: This street to the left is Liska Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this where the area of responsibility of the Vinko Skrobo ATG ends?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We won't need this photograph any more. I've finished. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, could we ask the witness to mark the areas of the responsibility of the Vinko Skrobo ATG?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [marks] I'd merely like to add that the position that was held by the unit at the command post, that is where the intervention group was, you cannot see it on this map. And it is about 500 or 600 metres beyond it, and I believe that the name of this street was Kalemova.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this explanation but all we were interested to know was the situation on the front line and it is as you pointed here, as you marked here?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We are tendering this, we do not know which number is it but you can give us the number later. Now, can we have D226? Can we now have the witness shown the report, Prosecutor's number is P511, the tenth binder, binder 10, 511.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seric, the interpreters are asking you to come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I thought my voice carried and therefore that there would be no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. The French booth has problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. NO can you see this report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: It's the 9th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it refers to what day, it covers what day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: The 8th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this report confirm, will you go through this text? Does it corroborate what you said just now, which part of the front line was manned by the Vinko Skrobo ATG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was the purpose of this and other reports of this kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Such reports were needed so that we could take stock of the situation on the front line on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what other task did the Vinko Skrobo ATG have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: The Vinko Skrobo ATG's task was to prevent the breakthrough of the BH Army's troops through the area of responsibility that was under -- that they manned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How strong was the Vinko Skrobo ATG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Well, it is difficult for me to say exactly how many men it had, because there were wounded and killed soldiers every day, but I think that this figure was ranged between 50 to 70 men, roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Honourable Court how many soldiers were in one shift on the front line and how many were on the reserve?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I believe that in one shift, there were about 14 to 15 men, and that on the reserve, there should have been also at least as many as on the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long was the shift for, that you manned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I think that one shift on the front line lasted for 12 hours, because all the units had the same practice, and that was a 12-hour shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where other soldiers were at the time? Were there any barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Some of them were in the headquarters, that was the intervention unit, and the next shift, and there were no barracks. Other soldiers would go to their own homes, they stayed at home. When they were not on the front line, when they were not manning the positions, they would be engaged in every day, private business. They would be with their families.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, during that leisure time, could you exercise effective control over them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No. It was not possible. It was not possible to control members of any one unit because they all had their private and family matters to tend to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. NO, do you know whether detainees were -- from Heliodrom were brought to units, including the Vinko Skrobo ATG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes. The detainees from the Heliodrom were brought to all the units in the city of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I please ask Madam Registrar to give the usher P5112 -- Exhibit P5112? Sorry. I believe this is also binder number 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me make a comparison. Is this an order dated 9 July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the meaning of this order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: The meaning of this order is exactly what it says in it, and that is that units could use detainees to work, to carry out some public works, just as it says in this order, and that the security of these detainees was granted by the person who took them over, who -- whose name is signed, or who signed such an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who issued this particular order? Who signed it? Don't, please, read any names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: This order, this approval, was issued by myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. NO, do you know how the detainees were taken over, how they were brought to these various units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: The person -- first of all I would receive a request from a unit and with the request, the person in charge would come to me, that person would be in charge of the security of these detainees, that person would then go to the Heliodrom military investigative prison, that person would take over those prisoners, and then the same person would return the same prisoners to the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have practically answered my next question, but still I'm going to put it to you for the record. Who was responsible for the detainees as per this and similar orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: The person who was responsible was the person who took them over. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. So the person who took them over was responsible for their safety and security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were detainees from Heliodrom taken exactly to these places that were mentioned in the orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Persons would be taken to the place which was found on the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did that take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. NO, could people, detainees, be taken from Heliodrom without this or such an order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I was not in Heliodrom, and I do not know. I think that they could not be taken without an approval or an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if the Vinko Skrobo ATG had its own, so to say, detainees excluding those from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally receive any complaint about the treatment of these people from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes. Only a few, couple of times, two or three times, I had complaints about some of the detainees being maltreated, but I don't remember that this was done by the ATG -- by the Vinko Skrobo ATG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
