utterances.text: Mr. NO, did you have any knowledge that the Vinko Skrobo ATG unit participated in the persecution of the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No, I did not have any such knowledge, but I would like to say that there were a number of cases in which individuals or groups of criminals would often pose as members of certain units to engage in illegal, dirty activities, and to mask their trail. I remember that I personally, on several occasions, bought such stories. I remember an occasion -- I think it was in June. I know that at the time, the HVO units were in the Northern Camp and that's why I believe it was prior to the 30th of June, when my duty operations officer in the headquarters called me, when I got there, a military police patrol was waiting for me there and they told me that Mr. Martinovic, with a large group of his members, tried to persecute Muslim civilians from one neighbourhood. I found that very suspicious. I hadn't known Mr. Martinovic for a long time, but he did not leave me with the impression of a person who was capable of doing something like that. I asked the policeman in that patrol whether they knew Mr. Martinovic, and they told me that it was on that occasion that they saw him for the first time. Then, together with a dozen other men and with a patrol of military police, I went to that neighbourhood. We didn't find anybody there, but the Muslim civilians who were visibly scared. I went to Mr. Martinovic's headquarters immediately. Mr. Martinovic at the time, I think, was overseeing the changeover of his troops on the front line. And then the policemen from that patrol realised that Mr. Martinovic, the real Mr. Martinovic, is not the same person that had introduced himself as Mr. Martinovic to them. And then it was then that we realised that it must have been a group of criminals posing as somebody else, and such instances were numerous at the time in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to another subject, events which took place on 17 September, 1993. Do you know what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: It's very difficult to remember all the dates, but I do remember 9 of May, I do remember 30 June, 17 September. I remember these very well. On that last day, members of the BH Army carried out one of the strongest attacks on HVO units in the city of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do in your area of responsibility in response to that operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: As every time when an attack was launched, I would order full combat readiness, and immediately, all the units, with the maximum strength, would be sent to the front line, and they -- then we would use all the available weapons, and responded to the attack, in order to prevent it, and in order to prevent the occupation of Mostar by the BH Army units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether a tank was engaged in that operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I believe that there was one tank which was engaged in that operation, along the entire length of the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that on that occasion, in that operation, detainees armed by wooden rifles, also participated in this operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Counsel, this is ridiculous. First of all, detainees never participated in any operation. It was a war. It was not a movie being filmed. And the stories about detainees and wooden rifles, I heard these stories some two or three years after the end of the war. These stories were launched by the AID in order to compromise the legal fight of the HVO to defend the city of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the final outcome of the operation? Were there any wounded, were there any casualties, anybody killed? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: The final outcome of the operation was that we preserved the front line, the defence line, but we had major casualties. We had major losses. I remember that we had between 15 and 20 of our men dead, and there were certainly over 50 injured, both civilians and troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for my last question I would like us to go to private session, if we may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, do you want to do your cross-examination or we break here and after that, you do your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Normally we would go until noon and then we would break. I can begin now and go for 15 minutes, Mr. President. If that would be the normal time that we would break. I'm ready to start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since we have 20 minutes early break, we prefer we break right now, and we'll resume at quarter past 12.00. So we will resume at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer. Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I was just in Defence counsel room and Laurent from the registry told me that it was his mistake. The meeting is tomorrow at 1.30, not today. I just found this out. I'm sorry, luckily, I ran into him but he just told me that five minutes ago, so I thought I would pass it on to you, Your Honours. Thank you very much. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, so in this case, we will sit according to our normal hours. Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, during the break we distributed materials for use in the cross-examination. I believe on the bench, the Trial Chamber has two groups of documents. One is in a binder, and the other is bound, but is outside. In addition, the third thing which is on the bench is a piece of paper from which I put the exhibits in the order on which we propose to go through them during the cross-examination. Judge Clark, the piece of paper does not -- I don't intend, and I don't think it would be possible nor do I intend to go into each of the documents that are found in the two groups but it is my hope to at least pass across the documents that are listed in the order on the one sheet of paper. The documents are tabbed at about every fifth document, I believe, to assist the Trial Chamber in getting to them more rapidly, in addition, during a certain part of the cross-examination, we will be referring to log books which are found in the bound or the binder itself. Cross-examined by Mr. Stringer:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, good afternoon, my name is Stringer I'm going to ask you some questions on behalf of the Prosecution. I'll ask at this time, the Registrar, or the usher provide the witness with the exhibits that are in folder number 1 on the top of the pile. These are P246.1 and P560.2. Witness, the document that I'm going to show you exist both English and also in your language. I've just got a couple of brief questions about these two documents. 246.1, sir, is a decision dated the 10th of February, 1993, from Bruno Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe we need to pass into private session for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, at about the time of this document, in August, 1993, did Mr. Vladimir Primorac then become the commander of the 1st Battalion of the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I can't remember that he was appointed as such. I can't really remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the 1st Battalion of the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during -- you've testified about the period of time, May of 1993, to the end of the conflict. I want to ask you, sir, specifically who were your superiors? And maybe just to speed things along, I'll put a couple of names to you. Was your direct superior Miljenko Lasic, who was the commander of the HVO Southeast Herzegovina operative zone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And his direct superior, then, would have been the chief of the HVO Main Staff, who, during these periods of time, would have been either Milivoj Petkovic, then Slobodan Praljak, and then toward the end of the conflict, Ante Roso?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, your subordinates, the persons directly subordinate to you, you testified about the ATG Vinko Skrobo. Was Mr. Martinovic a direct subordinate, sir, of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was no one in between -- could we go into private session, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we looked at one of these, a similar order earlier in your direct examination. This is a different one. Different date. But very similar. Do you recognise this, sir, as an order signed by you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I see it now. There were quite a number of such orders. I do not know what you mean by recognise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this appear to be an order signed by you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dated the 2nd of August, 1993. Now, just a preliminary question, because in your direct examination, you spoke about the ATG Vinko Skrobo, and I made a note to ask you whether the ATG Vinko Skrobo is the same thing as the ATG Mrmak, which figures on this document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes. It is one and the same unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what I'd like to do, Mr. Witness, is to, with this and some of the other documents, try to walk through some of the record keeping that relates to the release of prisoners from the Heliodrom. Taking -- you've got this document in front of you, 554.1. If you could take the next exhibit, which is Exhibit 434, out of the folder, now, just looking over that document, sir, would you agree with me that 434 appears to be a collection of many orders relating to the release of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: This is the first time I see this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's work with this for a few moments. I want to direct you, sir, to item number 87 on this exhibit, which is in front of you. Again without mentioning your name, sir, this appears to relate to an order, the ATG Mrmak of 2 August, 1993. And it's got a broj number ending with the number 703/93. My question, sir, is whether it appears, whether you would agree with me that item number 87 on this list corresponds to the previous exhibit, 554.1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Well, it looks like it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just trying to see if we can establish a connection between some of these orders issued by you and then the collection of orders that are found in 434. Now, the next document would be 562.1. And let's keep 434 on the table as well. I'm going to ask the witness to refer back to that. Witness, just taking a moment to look at this, it appears to me, sir, that this order signed by you relates back to item number 119 in Exhibit 434.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the next exhibit, 563.1, a document bearing your signature, dated 12 August, 1993, would this relate to item number -- would this relate to item number 134?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, Witness, just for the record, the three documents which we've just looked at which contain your signature all relate to the granting of permission to release detainees from the Heliodrom complex, the central military remand prison, release of those detainees to the ATG Mrmak? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I do not know what you mean by this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for the second time, Mr. Stringer affirms that this is an order to release prisoners to let them free, but it's not that. It means to release them to go to work. That is what the document says. He just -- just a moment, 434.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We agree that's what the document says. If I said anything different then I made a mistake. I certainly didn't mean to suggest that the witnesses were being set free or that the detainees were being set free. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Seric. Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before I object, for the record, for the record, we were looking at the document marked 562.1, but there is also document 562.11, and I'd merely like to check.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I don't have an answer for counsel. I can perhaps clear it up at the next break but 562.1 is the document that was put in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may proceed, and we'll check it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, just to be clear, because Mr. Seric may have heard something that's different than what I said in English, these documents that we have been looking at which bear your signature, these are all Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. orders in which you approved of the release of prisoners from the Heliodrom so that they could go to work, a work assignment for the ATG Mrmak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the ATG Mrmak at this time, sir, was under the command of Vinko Martinovic, Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the next exhibit is 603.2, and as we get to this one, Witness, let me ask you, if you were familiar with any of the record-keeping that took place at the Heliodrom when they actually came to take the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, Exhibit 603.2 is dated 17 September, 1993. This relates to an approval regarding the release of 30 prisoners or detainees from the Heliodrom to go work for the ATG Vinko Skrobo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just to continue with the process, sir, does this order relate or correspond to item number 284 in the other exhibit, which is P434? Item number 284.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So now recognising, sir, that you hadn't seen this document before, 434, sir, this would appear to be a document that lists many orders that came from you and others for the release of prisoners from the Heliodrom to go on work assignments with any number of different HVO units. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Well, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to try to take this one a next step further and ask you to look at the next exhibit, which is 601.1. And, we can set 434 aside for the moment. Sir, 601.1 is, I can represent, is a book that contains lists of the names of many prisoners. I'm going to ask you some questions about this and I'm going to direct you -- we can find our way through by looking at the page numbers which are stamped on the upper right-hand corner of the document. You see the stamped numbers on the upper right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we have just been looking at your order dated 17 September, 1993. This relates to the release of 30 detainees to the ATG Vinko Skrobo. What I'd like to do, sir, is to take you to page -- the page number with -- which ends with the letters 5272.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah. The last four digits are 5272. It's a double-sided document. Now, this page, sir, appears to relate or correspond to the date of 17 September, 1993. Do you see that written on the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the right-hand column, sir, do you see a reference to Vinko Skrobo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then as you move down the page, you move across to the following page, and you see a list of the names of 30 individuals there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to just note for the record, sir, ask you if you see, for example, item number 13, the name Hamdija Colakovic there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 19, did you see the name of Enes Pajo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 25 is Edin Tucakovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 28 is Aziz Colakovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then just under number 30, it appears, sir, that the person who signed for these prisoners is named Dinko Knezovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just looking at this document, sir, and again recognising that you haven't seen it before, it would appear to me, sir, that this list here corresponds to the release of prisoners that was approved by you on the same date, September 17, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. If the witness is reading something, and we can all read that, then it would be all right if he also read what it says at the end for that date, the 17th of September, because it says they were returned at 1940.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, if the Prosecution wants to know this information, he will ask the witness to confirm it. There is no need for you to point this out to us. Yes, Mr. Stringer. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I? But I agree with you, of course, but look at the date, the 27th, not the 17th, in the Croatian original, and I do not think that this is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could respond to all of this, these statements which are in my view at best saved for their cross-examination, all of this can be brought out in cross, I really don't see the point of just interjecting these sorts of issues during the direct examination when they can be clarified on cross, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You are in cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The redirect, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think all those issues could be addressed in the re-examination at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the next exhibit is 611.2. Exhibit 611.2. Yeah. Again just for the record, sir, does this appear -- this appears to be an order signed by you authorising the release of prisoners to the ATG Vinko Skrobo on the 27th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And now this time we will skip over Exhibit 434 but we'll move directly into Exhibit 601, which is this big book, and if I could, sir, direct you to the page that ends with the numbers 5331? Do you see first of all the date appearing at the top of that page, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the 28th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the left hand column of that page relates to 20 persons under the heading of the ATG Vinko Skrobo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, coming back to your order, Exhibit 611.2, now, I notice, I just ask you to look at the broj number, the reference number that appears on your order. Do you see that in the upper left-hand corner? It's 02-157/93.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is that same reference number found in the notations that you see just under the Vinko Skrobo reference in this book, 601.1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I don't know where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If you look at the ATG Vinko Skrobo here, then just directly beneath that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that, sir, does that reference appear to correspond directly to the same reference number that's found on your order of 27 September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next is Exhibit 703.3. Sir, if I could just ask you, can you look at that exhibit and tell me whether it is another order signed by you, for the release of prisoners to the ATG Vinko Skrobo on 1 December, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I did not sign this order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- so that someone else is signing over your name on this particular document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you able to recognise the signature appearing on this one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I notice that on Exhibit 434, which was the list of all the orders, there are a number of references to Mr. Vladimir Primorac. And I'd like to ask you now to look at the next exhibit, 551.1. Witness -- yes, you can take away the book. Witness, 551 is one exhibit, 551.1 is one exhibit but it consists of a lot of different orders, all of which appear over the name and/or the signature of Vladimir Primorac. I simply wanted to ask you to take a moment to look at those and to tell me whether these appear also to be orders issued by him or under his authority for release of prisoners to the ATG Mrmak or ATG Vinko Skrobo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: For the usher, we might want to have 434 ready.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. These are the orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And we will just take this with one and not all of them, just the first one, which is an order of Mr. Primorac dated 31 July, 1993, for the release of 30 prisoners from the Heliodrom taken to the ATG Mrmak. If I could direct you to item number 77, in Exhibit 434, just so that we can see whether this order also corresponds back to Exhibit 434.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next exhibit is 562.2. And while that one is coming, sir, let me ask you, do you know or do you recall that it was Stanko Bozic who was the warden or the administrator in charge of the central military remand prison at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you receive reports from Mr. Bozic from time to time concerning the treatment of prisoners and the things taking place in respect of prisoners who were being held at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Sometimes, but very rarely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this, sir, can you just take a moment to look at this and tell me whether this appears to be such a report made by Mr. Bozic, dated the 10th of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President I regret that we can't put these on the ELMO but virtually all of them bear the witness's name so I think it's just better not to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question, sir, is whether you recall receiving a report on or about the 10th of August, 1993, from Mr. Bozic concerning certain prisoners that had been wounded while in the custody of the ATG Mrmak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I've already answered, Mr. Prosecutor, that I rarely received these reports, and I can't -- I can really not recall the dates when I received any of them, because it was a long time ago altogether.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this appear to be a genuine or an authentic reports that would have been made by Mr. Bozic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I believe that the report is authentic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just for the record, this was a report sent not only to you but also to Mr. Coric, who was the commander of the military police for the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: According to this report, it does seem so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is 565.3. My question, sir, is whether this also appears to be a report by Mr. Bozic concerning some detainees that had been released to the ATG Mrmak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. We can withdraw those exhibits and move on to the next folder now. While the usher is getting the next folder, Witness, let me ask you just a couple questions in general terms. The HV, the Croatian Army, were units of the Croatian Army present in the Mostar or Herzegovina region during the time that you've testified about, May in 1993 until the end of the conflict with the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No, never were the HV units present in Herzegovina. There were only individuals and volunteers who were born in Herzegovina, who were members of the Croatian Army and when the war broke out in the area of Herzegovina, they volunteered and joined the HVO, but not as members of the Croatian Army but as those who were born in Herzegovina and came to defend their native land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next exhibit then is P638.2. Do you recognise that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: This is a form, all such documents are very similar, and this here is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is a document in which someone else signed above your name as the commander of -- let me -- I can withdraw that last phrase. Someone else signed this above your name, is that your testimony, sir? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is basically the same form that we've seen in all of the other documents that we've looked at previously that relate to the ATG Mrmak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, now this document in fact grants permission for a unit of the Croatian Army to take 45 prisoners from the Heliodrom, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No. There was no Croatian Army there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So whoever made this form, then, was mistaken as to who they were granting authority to? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes. It is correct that a mistake was made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go back to Exhibit 434, please, which contains the list of orders, I want to direct your attention, sir, to item number 381 in that exhibit. Sir, does Exhibit 434, item 381, contain the reference to the order that we are just looking at, sir, your order or an order issued on your name to release prisoners to a HV unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No. There was no HV in the area of Herzegovina. I don't know how could anybody write this, that it was the HV. These letters, HV, they don't mean that -- they don't stand for the Croatian Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They don't -- HV does not stand for the Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: It doesn't have to be the Croatian Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other units bearing the initials HV, sir, operating in your zone of responsibility that had some different origin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Within my -- the brigades, there were smaller units which were called differently and these reports were then given to their respective brigades. There were different names. Those were smaller organisational units at the level of a squad or a platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask the witness be shown Exhibit 566.2. This is in the binder, Mr. President. This is another one of these books, Witness, that we looked at already. I just want to direct your attention to some entries in these books. In 566.2, if you could go to page ending 4545, on that page, sir, in the left-hand column do you see a reference to HV, taking a couple prisoners out of the Heliodrom complex?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: It does say HV, but this HV does not mean that it was the Croatian Army, because there was no Croatian Army in the area at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 4574, do you have that page, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the reference to the HV 1 Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that it says so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that this is a unit of the Croatian Army that was present in Herzegovina, taking prisoners out of the Heliodrom to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No. The 1st Brigade of the Croatian Army was not there, and neither was any other unit of the Croatian Army, but again, I repeat that there were volunteers, people who left for Croatia from Western Herzegovina during the Croatian Army, 1991, during the time when the war was on in Croatia. After that, the same people who were natives of Western Herzegovina, returned from the Croatian Army and they came to fight with the Croatian Defence Council. There were no organised units of the Croatian Army in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is 567.1. Sir, if I could directs your attention Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to the page ending 5048? Now, sir, it appears to me there are references to three different HV units here removing prisoners from the Heliodrom on the 22nd of August, 1993. 2nd Brigade and also 1st Brigade. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I've already answered, in Herzegovina there were no units of the Croatian Army, so units of the Croatian Army could not take prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next exhibit is 645.1. Pages 5513 and 5514. Now, sir, on these two pages there are references to 1 Brigade HV, 2 Brigade HV, the date I believe the 29th of October, 1993. Sir, I understand or I assume that your answer will be the same. Based on everything we are looking at here, sir, do you allow for the possibility that discrete units of the HV were present down in the Herzegovina area and were using prisoners from the Heliodrom to -- on work assignments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No. There were never any HV units in the area of Herzegovina. The only ones who came to the area of Herzegovina were those people who were in the Croatian Army before that, whose relatives lived in Herzegovina, and as the war broke out in Herzegovina, these people returned as individuals. There were no units of the Croatian Army in Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can withdraw these exhibits now and pass on to the next folder. Witness, I want to talk to you for a couple of minutes about some of the other units that availed themselves of the prisoners in the Heliodrom complex. The next folder would be folder number 4, next exhibit is P565.5. Sir, did you also receive reports from Mr. Bozic about injuries and deaths of Muslim prisoners who had been in the custody of the 2nd Battalion of the HVO 2nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I have already told you that I received several reports from Mr. Bozic. Those reports were few and far between but I really can't remember which units availed themselves of these prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document, sir, does this appear to be another one of the reports made by Mr. Bozic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: This document does seem to be one of those reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next is Exhibit P605.1. Sir, this is a document, a report from Mr. Bozic dated 18 September, 1993. My question is whether, in fact, this is also one of the reports made by Mr. Bozic regarding the condition or treatment of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: This is a report which was made by Mr. Bozic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to look at this report for a moment, and we actually I think could put the first page on the ELMO of the English version. Now, sir, it appears here that you had issued an order releasing 70 detainees. Now, I'm sorry, we can't put that on the ELMO. I apologise. You issued an order for the release of 70 detainees to the 2nd Brigade, and that some five days later on the 18th of September, the detainees still had not returned. Mr. Bozic says that this is a brigade where detainees have been mistreated and beaten the most, have had a fairly large number of deaths among them, a copy of this report was sent to you by Mr. Bozic. Now, my question, sir, as we have seen a series of these orders, and I recognise you say that you didn't receive these sorts of reports often, but we've seen a series of these reports now in which Mr. Bozic is reporting on the wounding, killing, mistreatment of prisoners, and yet, sir, you continued to sign orders authorising these units to take prisoners out of the Heliodrom. My question is what measures did you take, sir, given your position, to ensure that prisoners were not mistreated and were not put in positions where they had to work under dangerous conditions? What did you do to stop that from happening after you received these reports?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Let me repeat once again. I received very few of these reports. I received them very rarely. And as soon as I received one, I would take measures, if we were to find out that any of the detainees were wounded, such a detainee would be given medical assistance, such a detainee would be taken to the general hospital in Mostar. If we were to learn which was very rarely, that some detainees were mistreated, I do allow that this may have happened, but only very rarely, then, together with the commander of that particular unit where -- which availed itself of the detainees, we would carry out an investigation and when we found out who participated in the mistreatment of the detainees, we would carry out an investigation and we would punish them. During this period, we carried out all sorts of investigations of all sorts of crimes, some of the perpetrators were discovered, some were not. However, in the archives of the military police, you can find documents showing that over 2.000 cases were processed for various crimes and out of these, over 70 per cent involved Croatian nationals, people of Croatian nation. However, Your Honours, you have to know that at that time, the situation in Mostar was chaotic, that the war was raging, that people were being killed every day, that people were being injured every day, that there were some several tens of thousands of people, Croat, who were expelled from the Eastern Mostar, from other parts of Herzegovina, from Central Bosnia. There were very frequent power cuts, there was not enough food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I apologise for interrupting but I think I need to try to bring you back to some of the questions that I've got to ask you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I interrupt very rarely but I believe it would only be fair to the witness if the explanation -- if he gives the full explanation. The witness is trying to explain everything to the Honourable Court. I think it would be only fair if we let him say what he has to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think this Trial Chamber has the right to cut short any answers by this witness. I think the first few lines of his previous answer is good enough. You may proceed, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President. I think I did allow the witness sufficient time to give a full explanation and I only interrupted when I thought that it was getting a bit beyond who was necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next two exhibits are 606.3, 607.4. Witness, these appear to be two orders over your signature, dated 20 September and 21 September, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is what I wanted to ask you about these two orders. These are both orders in which you're releasing prisoners to again the 2nd Battalion of the 2nd Brigade on the 20th and 21st. Now, we have already seen the report issued by Mr. Bozic on the 18th of September. That's Exhibit 605.1, in which he informs you and others that 70 prisoners, previously released to this unit, had not even been returned. He informs you that this unit is particularly brutal in dealing with the prisoners. He does this in his report of 18 September, and in fact, sir, rather than conducting an investigation, rather than taking measures to prevent this sort of thing from happening, in these two exhibits, you continue to approve and to grant the release of additional prisoners to the same unit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Prosecutor, can you -- can I please have the first document back? I believe that in the first document, does not refer to the 2nd Battalion of the 2nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 605.1. We could also give the witness 565.5.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, in this document, it says that 70 detainees have been released to the 2nd Brigade, not the 2nd Battalion of the 2nd Brigade and I wish to inform you that the 2nd Brigade had the 1st Battalion, the 2nd Battalion, the 3rd Battalion, the 4th Battalion. That the 2nd Brigade had four battalions. And that these are all each one of them entities unto themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back to 565.5, then. This is a report you received from Mr. Bozic dated 16 August, 1993, reporting to you the death of a prisoner, the wounding of additional prisoners, who had previously been released to the 2nd Battalion of the 2nd Brigade. So this is my question: Before releasing more prisoners to this unit in September of 1993, which is what you did on the 20th and 21st, before releasing those prisoners, what did you do to investigate these incidents that occurred in August of 1993? What did you do to make sure that these sorts of events didn't happen again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I've already answered that. So those detainees who had been harassed, then an investigation would be conducted, and the culprits who would be identified would then be punished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, as indicated in virtually all these reports, these are prisoners who are killed or wounded by fire coming from the other side of the confrontation line, the Muslim armed forces. Are those the culprits? Are those the persons that you viewed as responsible for the deaths and woundings of these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Well, all these detainees were wounded when fire was opened from the Muslim side, because the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina at that time shelled the city mercilessly, and then there would be some killed, not only amongst the detainees, there would also be some lethalities its among the civilian population because after all, it was a war, so there was shelling and gunfire every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was a war in which Muslim prisoners released on your authority were put directly into the middle of the confrontation line, used as human shields, tasked to move fortifications and sand bags, and it was in the course of those activities that they were wounded and killed, sir, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No. That is not so, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You deny that that occurred, sir? You deny that prisoners, Muslim prisoners from the Heliodrom were tasked to work in the confrontation lines along the Bulevar and Santiceva Street in Mostar? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Yes. Those things did not happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit 565.5. These men who were killed and wounded, Juso Jevic [phoen], Nedzad Kuvic [phoen], Jevo Colakovic [phoen] and Ibro Kriza [phoen]. Whatever came of the investigation into the wounding and killing of these men? What's the result? Are you able to tell us? Who was punished for this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: All these men were wounded in the depths of the city, and they were victims of the shells and fire that came from the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that as a result, sir, no one on the HVO side in your view was responsible for what happened to those men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I don't understand your question, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who on the HVO side is responsible for what happened to those men? Anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: In what sense do you mean when you say "responsible"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Criminally responsible.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: I have already answered that the detainees were killed during the shelling by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and by their snipers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can move to the next folder of exhibits, Mr. President. The next exhibit is 607.2. Sir, this exhibit actually includes a couple of documents, one is a handwritten note and then the other one appears to be written by Mr. Bozic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: And there is Mr. Bozic, too, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question, sir, before talking about this in greater detail, is it true, sir, that the Convicts Battalion, the Kaznjenicka Bojna, as well as the various ATGs had access to use of prisoners who were being held at the Heliodrom complex?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No, they did not have access.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, why not? Why not the Convicts Battalion? It appears to me that virtually all the other HVO units could use prisoners. Why not the KB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Units from Mostar, based on the application and our authorisation, and I do not see here that the Convicts Battalion had applied for an authorisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this report of Mr. Bozic indicates that on the 20th and 21st of September, 1993, a number of prisoners were released from the Heliodrom on the orders of Mr. Ivan Andabak, and then on the 21st of September, as ordered by Mr. Mladen Naletilic, Tuta. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No, I do not recall this. I am not aware of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And looking at the names of the persons being released in this document, sir, these appear to me to be all Croatian or Croat persons who were in the prison for having committed a number of serious crimes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: The names of these people do not ring any bell with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, sir, these prisoners were released just a day or two prior to the combat operation that is occurred in Rastani, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: You said that, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that combat operations between the HVO and the Armija took place in Rastani during 22nd, 23rd, 24th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember the exact date, but there were certain activities in Rastani, some fighting, some combat operations in Rastani, but I can't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 566.2? It's one of the books that we've already looked at, 566.2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I want to direct you to page ending with the numbers 4685.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ending 4685. Directing your attention sir to the top of the left-hand column do you see a reference there to Kaznjenicka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: It says here, Kaznjenicka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then just it appears to me, sir, that the date of this is the 21st of September, the date appears on the page opposite. Now, looking, sir, back at 607.2, Mr. Bozic's report, you see the names of the persons being released or identified by Mr. Bozic as having been released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: Well, it's Bozic who wrote this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And the names appearing on this report, sir, are -- match the names appearing on page 4685 of this logbook. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: The names in these two Bozic's reports, yes, they tally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So again, sir, I want to simply ask you, isn't it true that the Kaznjenicka Bojna, the Convicts Battalion, did have the ability or the authority to pull prisoners out of the Heliodrom for use on whatever tasks they deemed necessary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NO
utterances.text: No, not in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, I think it's time for us to have our break. Witness, I'm sorry, we have to keep you for another day in The Hague. I have to remind you that during your stay in The Hague, you are still under the oath, so please do not talk to anybody or let anybody talk to you about your testimony. We'll resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
